thread:
jess_support: Customer onboarding flagged: small startup hit repeated 429s during a weekend hackathon, says they were on the free plan but only ~6 concurrent requests. They also saw intermittent 401s after rotating keys. Can we triage? :thinking:

raj_engineer: Thanks. Do we have the org_id / account_id and a repro curl?

jess_support: Org: org_0x9f8. Customer pasted this curl and headers they saw.

jess_support: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_rotated" \ "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-2.7b","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 60
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 15

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

jess_support: They said the 401s started right after they rotated keys and some CI jobs retried aggressively.

oncall_kevin: Sounds like two things: 1) rotation created many short-lived tokens hitting our token-global bucket, 2) retry loop caused exhaustion. Free tier per-org burst cap is pretty conservative.

oncall_kevin: Can you confirm whether requests came from multiple API keys under the org or a single key?

jess_support: Customer claims multiple keys (~4) plus a few ephemeral CI tokens. They provided sample timestamps (attached in DM).

raj_engineer: If they rotated keys rapidly, we may have hit our ephemeral-key safety throttle which dedups across an org for free plans. That explains 429 even at low concurrency. The 401 is expected on the rotated key that hasn't been fully activated in our cache. Workaround: stop parallel rotations, use single primary key, wait 30s, retry with exponential backoff.

maria_sales: Customer is trying to run a 48-hour hackathon tomorrow and asked if we can temporarily raise their free-plan burst. They'd consider upgrading if we can give a short runway.

billing_ops: For free-tier exceptions we can do short temporary bursts but need org_id + timeframe + approval from sales. Can we get exact duration and expected QPS?

jess_support: Requested: 8 hours starting 09:00 UTC tomorrow, expected peak 20 QPS, mostly short generation calls. They want a one-off lift to avoid 429s.

raj_engineer: Engineering notes: temporary uplift is safe if we isolate to their org and enforce a hard kill if abuse detected. We can add a 10x burst allowance for 8 hours on a per-org override. Need ticket and billing approval.

maria_sales: I'll own the approval — will confirm billing approval and reply by EOD. If approved, can ops script the override?

billing_ops: OK please include org_0x9f8, requested window (2026-03-20T09:00:00Z to 2026-03-20T17:00:00Z), expected peak 20 QPS, contact email hello@startup.example. We'll log the exception and revert automatically.

oncall_kevin: Engineering mitigation for now: advise customer to 1) rotate keys sequentially, 2) implement 429 exponential backoff (start 200ms, cap 5s), 3) consolidate CI jobs onto a single stable key. Patch ready if we need to force per-key cooldown.

jess_support: I'll send these instructions to the customer and wait for Maria's approval note. Also created ticket #INC-7684 by deploy-bot. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Ticket created: INC-7684 — Temporary burst uplift request for org_0x9f8 (assigned to billing_ops).

maria_sales: FYI I'll copy the customer on the approval email and attach billing terms. If they upgrade to paid Dedicated we'll migrate them to a higher baseline.

raj_engineer: Follow-up: if we grant uplift, let's add a one-time trace hook to watch token churn and throttle triggers during the window. I can add lightweight logging to the org's quota controller.

billing_ops: Approved pending sales signoff. Please include a slip agreement (non-committal) and I'll apply the override.

jess_support: Great, I'll update thread when done and share the mitigation steps to customer.

maria_sales: Thanks — I'll ping when email sent. :handshake:
